activities_performed.description: Analyzed Controller-Executor architecture from research findings
findings: Clear separation of concerns: Dashboard (client) vs Bot pipeline (backend) vs Trading logic
Event-driven architecture via WebSocket live-data flow
Layered risk management with Kelly sizing and circuit breakers
Strategy factory pattern enables multi-strategy operations
Capital allocator separates reserve (80%) from tradable surplus (20%)

activities_performed.description: Generated improvement ideas for Controller-Executor pattern
ideas: Implement circuit breaker that pauses ALL strategies when any hits 5% DD (systemic risk)
Add strategy correlation matrix to prevent over-exposure to similar market regimes
Implement adaptive cooldown based on volatility regimes (shorter in low vol, longer in high vol)
Add real-time strategy performance weighting to capital allocator
Create unified configuration service for hot-reload of strategy parameters
Implement health check endpoints for each layer (dashboard, API, trading logic)
Add circuit breaker for excessive signal generation (prevent overtrading)
Implement gradual position scaling based on consecutive wins/losses

activities_performed.description: Optimized prompts for strategy signal generation and risk assessment
optimizations: Standardized signal format: {symbol, strategy, action, confidence, size, sl, tp, timestamp}
Created validation schema for signal objects before risk engine processing
Added metadata tracking for signal generation latency and source
Implemented signal deduplication within cooldown periods
Created fallback signal generation when primary strategy fails

activities_performed.description: Analyzed when to dispatch to specialized workers vs handle directly
conclusions: Handle architecture analysis and brainstorming directly in default profile
Dispatch to dev profile for implementation of architectural changes
Dispatch to research profile for validation of new risk models
Keep prompt engineering and signal standardization in default profile

architectural_decisions.decision: Maintain Controller-Executor separation but add cross-layer health monitoring
architectural_decisions.rationale: Current separation is sound; need better observability between layers

architectural_decisions.action: Implement systemic circuit breaker that correlates strategy performance
architectural_decisions.rationale: Prevent cascade failures when multiple similar strategies fail simultaneously
architectural_decisions.impact: Medium risk, high risk reduction potential

architectural_decisions.decision: Add adaptive cooldown based on recent signal quality and market volatility
architectural_decisions.rationale: Fixed 10s cooldown may be too aggressive or too conservative depending on conditions

architectural_decisions.recommendation: Dispatch to dev profile for implementation of health monitoring and systemic circuit breaker

limitations_identified: No cross-strategy correlation monitoring in current risk management
Fixed cooldown doesn't adapt to market conditions
Limited real-time visibility into strategy performance degradation
No automated failover when primary strategy underperforms
next_steps_for_dev: Implement health check endpoints for each architectural layer
Create systemic circuit breaker that monitors strategy correlation
Add adaptive cooldown mechanism based on volatility regimes
Create unified configuration service for hot parameter updates
